summary: The exact candidate fixes the primary unrecorded-event race and implements the opt-in loader-thread handoff, but its abort path is not failure-safe: a secondary exception while releasing layer events escapes the daemon before an ack is published or enqueue completion is marked, leaving later work able to hang.

tests.what_was_measured: On AMD Instinct MI350X/ROCm 7.2, waiting on the base's unrecorded LayerLoadingEvent allowed the consumer copy to observe 0/4096 producer values.
The exact candidate's CPU recorded gate produced 4096/4096 expected values with real GPU stream/event/copy ordering.
Exact candidate regression suite: 19 passed, 1 skipped.
Independent normal failure release/ack and FIFO shutdown drain: 2 tests passed.
A secondary event-record failure in the abort path escaped the loader loop; mark_enqueue_done was called 0 times and 0 acknowledgements were published.

gpu_evidence: AMD Instinct MI350X, gfx950, ROCm/HIP 7.2.26015; base 0/4096 versus candidate 4096/4096 expected values in the recorded-event ordering regression.
remaining_counterexamples: If producer_event.complete(), timing-event construction, event recording, or ack publication raises while handling a loader failure, the second exception escapes the daemon before mark_enqueue_done; no ack is published and slot rotation can block indefinitely.
remaining_limitations: No H100/CUDA device, TP=8 deployment, model weights, or cudaMemcpyBatchAsync direct-backend serving workload was available. H100 throughput and latency claims remain upstream measurements. The local GPU result validates ROCm event/copy ordering, not CUDA-specific performance or end-to-end serving throughput.
